From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

5. Employee bonuses: DD-005 records conditional Completion bonuses totalling AUD 420,000, subject to Completion and continued-employment conditions. Those amounts do NOT appear in the draft Completion funds flow. The disclosure does not state whether payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs apply.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation remains preliminary; the disclosure does NOT characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no loss amount.

7. Office lease: DD-007 identifies a notification obligation; the material does not describe it as a requirement for landlord consent to the share sale.

=== END SELLER DOCUMENTS ===

Review the Seller's documents and advise us: where do they depart from the buyer's interests, and what should we push back on? Identify the material issues yourself and give your reasoning. Then summarise your recommendations.

# Project Kestrel: Buyer Review of Seller's SPA Update and Disclosure Letter (SPA-003)

## 1. Headline view

The covering letter calls this a "fair and balanced package." It isn't. Taken together, the positions would leave Wattlebridge carrying most of the known risks with almost no remedy for them.

- **Known liabilities become non-claimable.** Broad general disclosure (Schedule 7) is combined with a constructive-knowledge bar (cl 8.3). The Disclosure Letter puts every identified problem into the data room. Under the Seller's drafting, those problems are then excluded from claims.
- **Fundamental, title, tax, indemnity and fraud protection all sit under one 20% cap and one 18-month window.** This comes from the catch-all limitation in cl 12.3/13 and cl 9.3/12.8/20.5, plus the proposal on fundamental warranties.
- **Several debt-like items fall outside the price mechanics.** These include Riverlark, the DD-005 bonuses, the Ironquay balance and possibly the Sandbar renewals. That is inconsistent with the agreed debt-free/cash-free basis.
- **The Seller Update's descriptions are not supported by its own Disclosure Letter.**

| Seller Update says | Disclosure Letter says |
|---|---|
| Bluefen "addressed" | No final consent; 11.3 conditions not evidenced as satisfied |
| DD-006 "not expected to be material" | Access, scope and notification obligations unknown; investigation preliminary |
| Sandbar renewals "ordinary-course" | Expressly does not say whether ordinary course, avoidable or accrued |
| Ironquay indemnity "adequate" | No payment receipt, no confirmatory assignment |
| Tax/IP "settled" | Not addressed at all |

We should treat the Update's descriptions as negotiating positions, not facts. We should say so in our response so the Seller cannot later argue we accepted them.

**Rough scale of known exposure:**

| Item | Amount (AUD) |
|---|---|
| Riverlark | 3,200,000 |
| Bonuses (before on-costs) | 420,000 |
| Ironquay open balance | 180,000 |
| Sandbar renewals | 330,000 |
| **Total** | **≈ 4,130,000** |

That is about 17% of the price, or 86% of the proposed AUD 4.8m cap, before any Bluefen, privacy, IP or tax exposure. If these items were left in the general warranty regime, they would nearly exhaust the cap on day one. They need to be dealt with through price, conditions and specific indemnities instead.

---

## 2. Material issues, in priority order

### Tier 1: Deal-critical

**1. Riverlark facility, about AUD 3.2m (cl 2/7)**

*The problem*
- A release "following Completion" is incompatible with a debt-free/cash-free deal.
- Change-control clause 8.1 is likely to be triggered by Completion itself. This could cause default or acceleration while the Company is in our hands.
- Until discharge, the security stays over Company assets. If the security extends to the shares, it is also a title problem.

*Our position*
- Repayment and discharge happen at Completion, as a Completion deliverable.
- The Seller provides:
  - a payoff letter stating the exact payout figure and per-diem amount;
  - executed deeds of release;
  - PPSR financing-change statements, or an irrevocable undertaking to lodge them within 1–2 business days;
  - return of any title documents.
- The payout is made from the purchase price through the funds flow and is deducted as Debt.
- Include a warranty that no other financial indebtedness or security exists.

**2. Bluefen consent: about 30% of revenue (cl 3/6.3)**

*The problem*
- Losing Bluefen would be a fundamental change to the value of the business.
- The Seller offers only "reasonable endeavours."
- It proposes that the condition is satisfied on any written consent. That would include a consent subject to the 11.3 conditions, or to new terms such as repricing, guarantees or shorter tenor, which could fall on the Buyer.

*Our position*
- Make this a condition precedent that is waivable only by the Buyer.
- The consent must be unconditional, or on conditions the Buyer approves in writing. Include evidence that the 11.3 conditions are satisfied.
- The consent must be in a form acceptable to the Buyer and must not change the commercial terms.
- Upgrade the Seller's obligation to "all reasonable endeavours," with information and participation rights for the Buyer.
- Add a sunset date with a Buyer walk-right.
- Fallback: a specific price adjustment, earn-out or retention tied to Bluefen continuing for 12 months.

**3. General disclosure (Schedule 7, DL 1.1–1.2) combined with Buyer knowledge (cl 8.3)**

*The problem*
- This is the central structural problem.
- The data room and public records are deemed disclosed.
- On top of that, anything "discoverable" by the Buyer or its advisers bars a claim. That is constructive knowledge, extended to everyone on our deal team.
- The effect is that the warranties largely become unenforceable for any issue that has been identified.

*Our position*
- **Delete the general disclosure of the data room.** Only matters specifically disclosed in the Disclosure Letter count, and only if fairly disclosed: in enough detail for a reasonable buyer to identify the nature, scope and financial effect of the matter.
- Data-room documents are disclosed only to the extent specifically cross-referenced, and only as to what they say on their face.
- Public records are limited to specified searches (ASIC, PPSR, court searches) on a specified date.
- No disclosure can be made against title, capacity or tax warranties.
- **Delete cl 8.3.** Replace it with a pro-sandbagging clause: the Buyer's rights are not affected by any investigation or knowledge, except matters fairly disclosed in the Disclosure Letter.
- **No updating of disclosure between signing and Completion that removes our claims.** Any new matter should give us a termination right or a claim.
- Note that the data-room cut-off was 22 September 2026, about six weeks ago. We need a bring-down of disclosure against the current position.

**4. Catch-all limitations (cl 12.3/13, cl 9.3/12.8/20.5) and fundamental warranties subject to the cap and time limit**

*The problem*
The phrase "applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise" would extend the 20% cap, the thresholds and the 18-month window to all of the following:
- title and capacity;
- tax;
- specific indemnities;
- leakage and price adjustment;
- restraints and covenants;
- Completion obligations;
- possibly fraud.

*Our position*

| Claim type | Cap | Time limit |
|---|---|---|
| General warranties | 20% (see item 7) | 18 months |
| Title/capacity | 100% of price, no thresholds | 7 years, or as long as permitted |
| Tax (warranties and indemnity) | 100% of price | 4–5 years post-Completion, aligned with ATO amendment and limitation periods, plus a buffer |
| Specific indemnities | Separate caps, or 100% | Their own longer periods |

- Leakage, price adjustment and covenant breaches sit outside the warranty limitations.
- **Fraud, dishonesty and wilful concealment are excluded from every limitation, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provision.**
- Narrow the non-reliance clause to representations outside the SPA and Disclosure Letter. It must not undercut the warranties or the information the Seller supplied for them.
- Reverse the default rule: limitations apply only to general Warranty Claims unless expressly extended.

### Tier 2: Specific indemnities and price mechanics

**5. DD-005 bonuses: AUD 420,000 plus on-costs**

*The problem*
- Calling these "a matter for the Seller" is wrong. The obligation is the Company's, and Completion triggers it.
- If the bonuses are omitted from the funds flow, the Company pays them after Completion.
- On top of the bonuses themselves there are:
  - PAYG withholding;
  - payroll tax (NSW);
  - possibly superannuation guarantee, depending on whether the bonuses count as ordinary time earnings;
  - workers' compensation on-costs.

*Our position*
- Treat the full amount, including all on-costs, as Transaction Costs/Debt deducted from the price.
- Pay it through Company payroll at or immediately after Completion, from a funded amount.
- Add a specific indemnity for any shortfall.
- The continued-employment conditions should not mean we fund bonuses that the Seller negotiated.

**6. Ironquay SOW3 intellectual property (cl 11.1)**

*The problem*
- DD-004 cl 7.3 makes transfer of the SOW3 Project Materials conditional on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee.
- AUD 180,000 is recorded as open, and there is no receipt and no confirmatory assignment.
- The Company may therefore not own the SOW3 materials. If they are embedded in the product, this is a core IP gap.
- An indemnity "limited to the SOW3 payment" covers the cheapest part of the risk and none of the rest:
  - infringement claims;
  - injunctions;
  - re-development costs;
  - customer claims.

*Our position*
- Completion deliverables:
  - evidence of cleared payment, or payment through the funds flow, with any unpaid amount treated as Debt;
  - an executed confirmatory assignment from Ironquay;
  - moral rights consents for the relevant authors.
- A full specific indemnity for all Loss arising from any failure of the Company to own the SOW3 materials. It should sit outside the general cap and thresholds, with a period of at least 3–5 years.
- Strengthen the IP warranties: ownership, no third-party claims, contractor assignments.

**7. DD-006 data export incident: about 1,240 records**

*The problem*
- The records include names, business emails, roles and timestamps.
- Whether anyone accessed the file, the scope, and whether notification is required are all unresolved as at 22 September.
- Under the Privacy Act 1988 (Cth) Notifiable Data Breaches scheme, an entity that suspects an eligible data breach must carry out a reasonable assessment, generally within 30 days. That window may already have passed, which would itself be a compliance issue.
- Further exposure includes:
  - OAIC regulatory risk and penalties;
  - customer contract and confidentiality claims;
  - the newer statutory tort for serious invasions of privacy, depending on facts and timing.
- Because the incident is disclosed, it would be carved out of the warranties. A specific indemnity is therefore the only real protection.

*Our position*
- Request immediately:
  - the incident timeline;
  - the forensic or IT report;
  - the NDB assessment and whether the OAIC or affected individuals were notified;
  - access logs for the download link;
  - customer contractual notification obligations.
- Pre-Completion covenant: complete the assessment, make any required notifications, and consult the Buyer.
- A specific indemnity for all Loss, including regulatory penalties to the extent indemnifiable at law, remediation costs, notification costs and third-party claims. It should sit outside the general limitations.
- Consider making this a condition if the facts remain unclear at signing.

**8. Sandbar renewals: 3 × AUD 110,000, AUD 330,000 in total**

*The problem*
- The Disclosure Letter itself flags that the three renewals must be "read together for timing/scope" and are "related." That points to a single arrangement split into three.
- The split may have been used to stay under a material-contract threshold, a board-approval limit or a conduct-of-business covenant.
- "Related supplier" may mean a related party of the Seller. If so, value may be leaking to the Seller.
- The Seller describes the renewals as ordinary course. Its own disclosure declines to say so.

*Our position*
- Request:
  - all three contracts;
  - approval records;
  - the relationship between Sandbar and Harbourglass or its affiliates;
  - termination rights;
  - prepayment and accrual status.
- Depending on the answers:
  - treat committed or prepaid amounts outside the ordinary course as Debt or Leakage;
  - require termination or variation before Completion at the Seller's cost; or
  - obtain a specific indemnity.
- Add the renewals to the locked-box or Leakage provisions, if relevant, and to the conduct-of-business restrictions.

### Tier 3: Other points

**9. Title (DD-012)**

*The problem*
- A share register alone is not enough. The Disclosure Letter itself says the Buyer has not verified title.

*Our position*
- Full title and capacity warranties, which are not disclosable against.
- An ASIC company extract and a PPSR search against the shares and the Seller.
- Confirm there are no options, convertibles, SAFEs or employee equity. This is common in VC-backed companies and should be cross-checked against DD-005.
- Releases of any share security, which links back to Riverlark.

**10. Tax and IP "settled under the general regime"**

*Our position*
- Reject. We need a standalone tax indemnity covering pre-Completion tax, including payroll tax and super on the bonuses, plus full tax warranties.
- Both should carry the caps and periods in item 4.
- IP warranties should be strengthened as described in item 6.

**11. Thresholds (cl 12.2)**

*The problem*
- The AUD 250,000 basket is drafted as a deductible ("only the excess"). We should resist that.

*Our position*
- A tipping basket: once claims cross the threshold, we recover from dollar one.
- Consider reducing the basket to about AUD 120,000–180,000 (0.5–0.75%).
- The de minimis should be about AUD 10,000–15,000, with related claims aggregated.
- No thresholds should apply to fundamental, tax or indemnity claims.

**12. General cap of 20%**

- This is within the market range for general warranties, but only if items 3, 4 and 6–8 are fixed.
- We could press for 30% or more, or treat the cap as a trade.
- If W&I insurance is being considered, the structure changes. We should decide that early.

**13. Seller covenant strength**

*The problem*
- Harbourglass is a venture vehicle and may distribute proceeds soon after Completion. Claims could then be uncollectable.

*Our position*
- Seek an escrow or retention of about 10–15% for 18 months, plus specific retentions for the Bluefen, DD-006 and Ironquay exposures.
- Alternatively, a guarantee from a creditworthy fund entity.

**14. Lease (DD-007) and Mossvale (DD-009)**

- These are lower risk on the Seller's description, but we should check the actual clauses.
- For the lease: confirm notice is only a notification and is given in time.
- For Mossvale: confirm the restriction does not deem a change of control to be an assignment.
- Include both in the warranties on change-of-control and consents.

**15. DL 1.4 and DL 11**

- The non-admission clause (1.4) is acceptable only if it does not dilute fair disclosure.
- DL 11 tries to put the burden of evaluating the disclosures on us. Our SPA should state that the warranties are given notwithstanding.

---

## 3. Summary of recommendations

1. **Reject general disclosure and cl 8.3 outright.** Require specific, fair disclosure only, a pro-sandbagging clause, and a bring-down of disclosure to the current date.
2. **Ring-fence the limitations.** Title, capacity and tax at 100% with long periods; specific indemnities on separate terms; fraud excluded from everything; the catch-all reversed; non-reliance narrowed.
3. **Make the price genuinely debt-free/cash-free at Completion.**
   - Riverlark repaid and released at Completion through the funds flow.
   - The AUD 420,000 bonuses plus all on-costs deducted.
   - The Ironquay balance paid or deducted.
   - Committed Sandbar amounts treated as Debt or Leakage where justified.
4. **Bluefen as a Buyer-waivable condition precedent.** Unconditional or Buyer-approved consent, evidence that 11.3 is satisfied, all reasonable endeavours, a sunset date and a walk-right. Price protection as fallback.
5. **Specific indemnities outside the cap** for Ironquay IP ownership (full Loss, not just the fee) and the DD-006 incident, backed by Completion deliverables (assignment, moral rights consents) and pre-Completion covenants (NDB assessment and notification).
6. **Sandbar:** diligence the related-party link and the contract splitting before we agree any treatment.
7. **Title:** fundamental warranties plus our own ASIC and PPSR verification and a check of the equity instruments.
8. **Thresholds and cap:** tipping basket, lower de minimis with aggregation, no thresholds on fundamental, tax or indemnity claims. Treat the 20% general cap as a possible trade.
9. **Security for claims:** escrow or retention, or a fund guarantee.
10. **In our cover note,** record that we do not accept the Seller Update's descriptions of Bluefen, DD-006, Sandbar, Ironquay or tax/IP.

## 4. Immediate information requests

- Riverlark payoff letter and full security list (including whether the shares are secured).
- Bluefen clauses 11.2–11.3 in full, and the status of the consent request.
- Ironquay payment records from bank statements, and the SOW3 deliverables map showing what is in the product.
- DD-006 forensic and assessment file, and any OAIC or customer communications.
- Sandbar contracts, approvals and ownership.
- DD-005 bonus letters and a payroll tax and super analysis.
- Full DD-007 and DD-009 clauses.
- Cap table and equity instruments.

*Caveat:* This review is based only on the Seller's summaries. We have not reviewed the underlying DD-002 to DD-012 documents. The positions above should be checked against those documents and the full SPA draft before we issue the mark-up.

  - workers' compensation on-costs.

*Our position*
- Treat the full amount, including all on-costs, as Transaction Costs/Debt deducted from the price.
- Pay it through Company payroll at or immediately after Completion, from a funded amount.
- Add a specific indemnity for any shortfall.
- The continued-employment conditions should not mean we fund bonuses that the Seller negotiated.

**6. Ironquay SOW3 intellectual property (cl 11.1)**

*The problem*
- DD-004 cl 7.3 makes transfer of the SOW3 Project Materials conditional on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee.
- AUD 180,000 is recorded as open, and there is no receipt and no confirmatory assignment.
- The Company may therefore not own the SOW3 materials. If they are embedded in the product, this is a core IP gap.
- An indemnity "limited to the SOW3 payment" covers the cheapest part of the risk and none of the rest:
  - infringement claims;
  - injunctions;
  - re-development costs;
  - customer claims.

*Our position*
- Completion deliverables:
  - evidence of cleared payment, or payment through the funds flow, with any unpaid amount treated as Debt;
  - an executed confirmatory assignment from Ironquay;
  - moral rights consents for the relevant authors.
- A full specific indemnity for all Loss arising from any failure of the Company to own the SOW3 materials. It should sit outside the general cap and thresholds, with a period of at least 3–5 years.
- Strengthen the IP warranties: ownership, no third-party claims, contractor assignments.

**7. DD-006 data export incident: about 1,240 records**

*The problem*
- The records include names, business emails, roles and timestamps.
- Whether anyone accessed the file, the scope, and whether notification is required are all unresolved as at 22 September.
- Under the Privacy Act 1988 (Cth) Notifiable Data Breaches scheme, an entity that suspects an eligible data breach must carry out a reasonable assessment, generally within 30 days. That window may already have passed, which would itself be a compliance issue.
- Further exposure includes:
  - OAIC regulatory risk and penalties;
  - customer contract and confidentiality claims;
  - the newer statutory tort for serious invasions of privacy, depending on facts and timing.
- Because the incident is disclosed, it would be carved out of the warranties. A specific indemnity is therefore the only real protection.

*Our position*
- Request immediately:
  - the incident timeline;
  - the forensic or IT report;
  - the NDB assessment and whether the OAIC or affected individuals were notified;
  - access logs for the download link;
  - customer contractual notification obligations.
- Pre-Completion covenant: complete the assessment, make any required notifications, and consult the Buyer.
- A specific indemnity for all Loss, including regulatory penalties to the extent indemnifiable at law, remediation costs, notification costs and third-party claims. It should sit outside the general limitations.
- Consider making this a condition if the facts remain unclear at signing.

**8. Sandbar renewals: 3 × AUD 110,000, AUD 330,000 in total**

*The problem*
- The Disclosure Letter itself flags that the three renewals must be "read together for timing/scope" and are "related." That points to a single arrangement split into three.
- The split may have been used to stay under a material-contract threshold, a board-approval limit or a conduct-of-business covenant.
- "Related supplier" may mean a related party of the Seller. If so, value may be leaking to the Seller.
- The Seller describes the renewals as ordinary course. Its own disclosure declines to say so.

*Our position*
- Request:
  - all three contracts;
  - approval records;
  - the relationship between Sandbar and Harbourglass or its affiliates;
  - termination rights;
  - prepayment and accrual status.
- Depending on the answers:
  - treat committed or prepaid amounts outside the ordinary course as Debt or Leakage;
  - require termination or variation before Completion at the Seller's cost; or
  - obtain a specific indemnity.
- Add the renewals to the locked-box or Leakage provisions, if relevant, and to the conduct-of-business restrictions.

### Tier 3: Other points

**9. Title (DD-012)**

*The problem*
- A share register alone is not enough. The Disclosure Letter itself says the Buyer has not verified title.

*Our position*
- Full title and capacity warranties, which are not disclosable against.
- An ASIC company extract and a PPSR search against the shares and the Seller.
- Confirm there are no options, convertibles, SAFEs or employee equity. This is common in VC-backed companies and should be cross-checked against DD-005.
- Releases of any share security, which links back to Riverlark.

**10. Tax and IP "settled under the general regime"**

*Our position*
- Reject. We need a standalone tax indemnity covering pre-Completion tax, including payroll tax and super on the bonuses, plus full tax warranties.
- Both should carry the caps and periods in item 4.
- IP warranties should be strengthened as described in item 6.

**11. Thresholds (cl 12.2)**

*The problem*
- The AUD 250,000 basket is drafted as a deductible ("only the excess"). We should resist that.

*Our position*
- A tipping basket: once claims cross the threshold, we recover from dollar one.
- Consider reducing the basket to about AUD 120,000–180,000 (0.5–0.75%).
- The de minimis should be about AUD 10,000–15,000, with related claims aggregated.
- No thresholds should apply to fundamental, tax or indemnity claims.

**12. General cap of 20%**

- This is within the market range for general warranties, but only if items 3, 4 and 6–8 are fixed.
- We could press for 30% or more, or treat the cap as a trade.
- If W&I insurance is being considered, the structure changes. We should decide that early.

**13. Seller covenant strength**

*The problem*
- Harbourglass is a venture vehicle and may distribute proceeds soon after Completion. Claims could then be uncollectable.

*Our position*
- Seek an escrow or retention of about 10–15% for 18 months, plus specific retentions for the Bluefen, DD-006 and Ironquay exposures.
- Alternatively, a guarantee from a creditworthy fund entity.

**14. Lease (DD-007) and Mossvale (DD-009)**

- These are lower risk on the Seller's description, but we should check the actual clauses.
- For the lease: confirm notice is only a notification and is given in time.
- For Mossvale: confirm the restriction does not deem a change of control to be an assignment.
- Include both in the warranties on change-of-control and consents.

**15. DL 1.4 and DL 11**

- The non-admission clause (1.4) is acceptable only if it does not dilute fair disclosure.
- DL 11 tries to put the burden of evaluating the disclosures on us. Our SPA should state that the warranties are given notwithstanding.

## 3. Summary of recommendations

1. **Reject general disclosure and cl 8.3 outright.** Require specific, fair disclosure only, a pro-sandbagging clause, and a bring-down of disclosure to the current date.
2. **Ring-fence the limitations.** Title, capacity and tax at 100% with long periods; specific indemnities on separate terms; fraud excluded from everything; the catch-all reversed; non-reliance narrowed.
3. **Make the price genuinely debt-free/cash-free at Completion.**
   - Riverlark repaid and released at Completion through the funds flow.
   - The AUD 420,000 bonuses plus all on-costs deducted.
   - The Ironquay balance paid or deducted.
   - Committed Sandbar amounts treated as Debt or Leakage where justified.
4. **Bluefen as a Buyer-waivable condition precedent.** Unconditional or Buyer-approved consent, evidence that 11.3 is satisfied, all reasonable endeavours, a sunset date and a walk-right. Price protection as fallback.
5. **Specific indemnities outside the cap** for Ironquay IP ownership (full Loss, not just the fee) and the DD-006 incident, backed by Completion deliverables (assignment, moral rights consents) and pre-Completion covenants (NDB assessment and notification).
6. **Sandbar:** diligence the related-party link and the contract splitting before we agree any treatment.
7. **Title:** fundamental warranties plus our own ASIC and PPSR verification and a check of the equity instruments.
8. **Thresholds and cap:** tipping basket, lower de minimis with aggregation, no thresholds on fundamental, tax or indemnity claims. Treat the 20% general cap as a possible trade.
9. **Security for claims:** escrow or retention, or a fund guarantee.
10. **In our cover note,** record that we do not accept the Seller Update's descriptions of Bluefen, DD-006, Sandbar, Ironquay or tax/IP.

## 4. Immediate information requests

- Riverlark payoff letter and full security list (including whether the shares are secured).
- Bluefen clauses 11.2–11.3 in full, and the status of the consent request.
- Ironquay payment records from bank statements, and the SOW3 deliverables map showing what is in the product.
- DD-006 forensic and assessment file, and any OAIC or customer communications.
- Sandbar contracts, approvals and ownership.
- DD-005 bonus letters and a payroll tax and super analysis.
- Full DD-007 and DD-009 clauses.
- Cap table and equity instruments.

*Caveat:* This review is based only on the Seller's summaries. We have not reviewed the underlying DD-002 to DD-012 documents. The positions above should be checked against those documents and the full SPA draft before we issue the mark-up.
